faq.q: What is the salary of a BCS Administration cadre officer?
faq.a: New officers join at Grade 9. Under the new 9th pay scale the starting basic pay is listed at BDT 44,000 (old scale BDT 22,000), paid in stages up to July 2027, plus allowances. Senior grades rise to BDT 1,56,000 basic at Grade 1. Check the gazette, as figures were checked on 18 Nov 2026.

faq.q: What does an Assistant Commissioner (Land) do?
faq.a: An AC (Land) handles land administration at an upazila: mutation (namjari), land development tax and management of government land. As an Executive Magistrate the officer also runs mobile courts and can impose fines and punishments under the law.

faq.q: How many Administration cadre posts are there?
faq.a: BPSC advertised 200 Administration posts in the 47th BCS and 200 again in the 50th BCS. The 50th had 290,951 applicants overall for 1,755 cadre posts, so competition is very high.

faq.q: Do I need a specific degree for BCS Administration?
faq.a: Administration is a general cadre, so any recognised bachelor's degree (or equivalent) usually qualifies. Check the exact degree and result rules in the circular.

faq.q: How long is probation for a new Assistant Commissioner?
faq.a: Two years, after which officers are confirmed on passing assessments. Probation is taken seriously: in November 2025 three probationary Assistant Commissioners of the 43rd batch were removed during basic training.

faq.q: How do promotions work in the Administration cadre?
faq.a: Officers move from Assistant Secretary to Senior Assistant Secretary, then Deputy Secretary, Joint Secretary, Additional Secretary and Secretary under the Promotion Rules of 2002. For Deputy Secretary an officer needs at least 10 years' service and five years as Senior Assistant Secretary; for Joint Secretary, five years as Deputy Secretary. Training is a condition, and timelines can run longer than the rules suggest.

faq.q: Can I choose Administration after passing BCS?
faq.a: You give cadre choices on the application form. Allocation depends on your merit position, your choices and the vacancies, so give realistic second and third choices that you genuinely want.

faq.q: Does BCS Administration need a CV or career objective?
faq.a: BCS does not choose by CV, and marks decide. A short honest profile helps in the viva and in backup applications. For example: 'Public Administration graduate preparing for the BCS general cadre, with experience leading a student relief team and strong Bangla and English writing.'

body_md:
**By [Daloyar Hassan Shishir](https://www.dhshishir.com)** · Career consultant, founder of Career Solutions and HereWeGrow · Facts last checked: 18 November 2026 · Last updated: 19 November 2026

> **Quick answer:** BCS (Administration) is the generalist cadre of the Bangladesh Civil Service. New officers join as Assistant Commissioner in the field (many serve as AC Land, or "ACland") or as Assistant Secretary in the Secretariat, at Grade 9. The starting basic pay under the new 9th pay scale is listed at BDT 44,000, phased in up to July 2027. BPSC advertised 200 Administration posts in both the 47th and the 50th BCS, so competition is intense. The path leads from Senior Assistant Secretary to Deputy Secretary, Joint Secretary, Additional Secretary and Secretary.

## Key facts: BCS Administration cadre (as of 18 November 2026)

| Question | Short answer |
|---|---|
| Entry post | Assistant Commissioner (field) or Assistant Secretary (Secretariat) |
| Entry grade | Grade 9 |
| First posting | Usually Assistant Commissioner in the field, on a 2-year probation |
| Starting basic pay | BDT 44,000 (new 9th scale, phased in); old scale BDT 22,000 |
| Posts in recent exams | 200 in the 47th BCS; 200 in the 50th BCS |
| Who decides | BPSC recruits; the Ministry of Public Administration posts and promotes |
| Minimum education | A bachelor's degree or equivalent (check the circular) |
| Age | 21 to 32 on the cut-off date |

## What does the Administration cadre do?

The Administration cadre runs the government's general machinery in two settings.

**Field administration.** This is the district and upazila level. The posts, from the bottom, are Assistant Commissioner, Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO, who is also a Senior Assistant Commissioner), Additional Deputy Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner (DC) and Divisional Commissioner. Many officers in these posts are also Executive Magistrates.

**Secretariat.** This is the ministry level, where policy files are drafted and decided. The ladder is Assistant Secretary, Senior Assistant Secretary, Deputy Secretary, Joint Secretary, Additional Secretary and Secretary.

### AC (Land): the job most new officers do first

Many new Assistant Commissioners are posted as AC (Land) at an upazila. The post covers mutation (namjari), land development tax, management of government land and other land administration work. Officers also run mobile courts as Executive Magistrates and can impose fines and punishments under the law. At an orientation for new AC (Land) officers in September 2025, the land adviser called the AC (Land) the second most important person in an upazila's administration, after the UNO.

Before posting, newly appointed Assistant Commissioners (Land) attend a Basic Land Management Course at the Land Administration Training Centre in Dhaka.

## What is the career ladder from Assistant Commissioner to Secretary?

| Level | Field administration | Secretariat | Pay grade |
|---|---|---|---|
| Entry | Assistant Commissioner | Assistant Secretary | 9 |
| Senior scale | Senior Assistant Commissioner / UNO | Senior Assistant Secretary | 6 |
| Mid-senior | Additional DC | Deputy Secretary | 5 |
| Senior | Deputy Commissioner (DC) | Joint Secretary | 3 to 4 |
| Top | Divisional Commissioner | Additional Secretary, Secretary | 2 and 1 |

*A simplified map. DC and other field posts sit across the Deputy Secretary and Joint Secretary level, and officers move between field and Secretariat.*

**Promotion rules to know:**

- To be considered for Deputy Secretary, an officer needs at least 10 years in service and five years as Senior Assistant Secretary, plus a benchmark score of 83 or above.
- To be considered for Joint Secretary, an officer must have served at least five years as Deputy Secretary.
- Promotions to these ranks are governed by the Promotion Rules of 2002 and decided through selection boards. Under the rules, the Administration cadre gets a majority share of senior posts (for example 70 per cent of Joint Secretary posts) and officers of the other 25 cadres share the rest. This is a long-running dispute between cadres.
- **Training is a condition.** Deputy Secretaries attend a 10-week Advanced Course on Administration and Development (ACAD), including a short overseas segment.
- Reports say hundreds of eligible officers are often waiting for promotion at each level, so timelines can run longer than the rules suggest.

## How many Administration posts are there, and how competitive is it?

| Exam | Administration posts | Total cadre posts |
|---|---|---|
| 47th BCS (circular Dec 2024) | 200 | 3,487 |
| 50th BCS (circular Nov 2025) | 200 | 1,755 |

In the 50th BCS, 290,951 people applied for the preliminary, 12,385 passed, and 6,165 passed the written. For Administration alone, 200 posts against 290,951 applicants is roughly 1 post for every 1,450 applicants, although candidates compete across many cadres. Cadre allocation depends on your merit position, the cadre choices you gave on the application form and the vacancies.

**Visual: Administration posts in recent BCS**

| Exam | Posts | Visual |
|---|---|---|
| 47th BCS | 200 | ████████████████████ |
| 50th BCS | 200 | ████████████████████ |

## What is the salary and what are the benefits (2026)?

The 9th National Pay Scale was approved by cabinet on 31 August 2026 and takes effect from 1 July 2026. Basic pay is raised in stages up to July 2027 (reports describe three or four steps), so your early pay is below the final figure. Allowances are reset from January 2028.

| Level | Grade | Old basic (BDT) | New basic (BDT) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Assistant Commissioner / Assistant Secretary | 9 | 22,000 | 44,000 |
| Senior Assistant Secretary | 6 | 35,500 | 71,000 |
| Deputy Secretary | 5 | 43,000 | 86,000 |
| Joint Secretary | 3 | 56,500 | 1,13,000 |
| Additional Secretary | 2 | 66,000 | 1,32,000 |
| Secretary | 1 | 78,000 | 1,56,000 |

*Source note: these figures come from a teacher-portal summary of the new scale, not the gazette. The Daily Star separately confirms Grade 1 at BDT 1,56,000. Always check the gazette before you quote a figure to someone.*

**Benefits beyond basic pay:**

- House rent and medical allowance, with house rent depending on where you are posted.
- Festival bonuses at both Eids and the Bengali New Year allowance.
- Government service rules for leave, pension and provident fund.
- Training in Bangladesh and abroad, and a clear promotion ladder.
- A public role that carries real authority and real responsibility.

## What happens in the first two years?

- **Foundation training** for new BCS entrants is run by the Bangladesh Public Administration Training Centre (BPATC) at Savar.
- **Probation:** new Assistant Commissioners serve a 2-year probation and are confirmed after assessments.
- **Probation is real.** In November 2025 the Ministry of Public Administration removed three probationary Assistant Commissioners of the 43rd batch from service during basic training.
- **Land course:** before an AC (Land) posting you complete the Basic Land Management Course.

## Skills that make a strong Administration officer

| Skill | Why it matters | Demand |
|---|---|---|
| Land and revenue basics | AC (Land) work is daily mutation and tax | █████ |
| Magistracy and mobile court procedure | Executive Magistrate duties | ████ |
| Official writing (notes, drafts, letters) | Secretariat work is file based | █████ |
| Integrity and resisting pressure | Public trust | █████ |
| Leadership and people handling | You lead staff and mediate disputes | ████ |
| Local government knowledge | UNO and DC offices | ███ |
| Digital service delivery | Online land and citizen services | ███ |
| Crisis coordination | Floods, cyclones, relief | ███ |

*Bars show our reading of the role, not a survey.*

## How do I get in? The exam path

The Administration cadre uses the general BCS exam: a 200-mark MCQ preliminary, a 900-mark written exam (Bangla 200, English 200, Bangladesh Affairs 200, International Affairs 100, Mathematical Reasoning and Mental Ability 100, General Science and Technology 100) and a 100-mark viva. Read the full exam guide in our BCS overview.

**To aim for Administration:**

1. Put it first on your cadre choice list when you apply, with realistic second and third choices.
2. Build writing speed early. The written exam decides most of the rank.
3. Study Bangladesh Affairs well, with extra attention to the Constitution, local government and land administration.
4. Practise viva questions about your own district and about public service, not just textbook answers.
5. Keep a plan B; most candidates need more than one round.

## Free ways to build these skills

- **Syllabus and past circulars:** [bpsc.gov.bd](https://www.bpsc.gov.bd).
- **Service rules and notices:** [mopa.gov.bd](https://mopa.gov.bd) (Ministry of Public Administration).
- **What officers learn after joining:** [bpatc.gov.bd](https://bpatc.gov.bd).
- **Bangla e-learning:** [muktopaath.gov.bd](https://muktopaath.gov.bd).
- **Daily practice:** read one national daily and write a 150-word summary of one issue every day.

## Study support and scholarships (check each official site)

- **Chevening (UK):** [chevening.org](https://www.chevening.org) for a funded master's.
- **Commonwealth Scholarships:** [cscuk.fcdo.gov.uk](https://cscuk.fcdo.gov.uk).
- **DAAD (Germany):** [daad.de](https://www.daad.de/en/).
- **Fulbright (USA):** through the US Embassy in Dhaka.
- **JDS (Japan):** [jds-scholarship.org](https://www.jds-scholarship.org), a programme for government officials. Check whether Bangladesh is currently open.

## Long-term career timeline

| Years | Typical title | What to master |
|---|---|---|
| 0 to 1 | Probationary Assistant Commissioner | Foundation training, land course, magistracy |
| 2 to 5 | AC (Land), Senior Assistant Commissioner or UNO, Assistant Secretary | Land, courts, upazila coordination, file writing |
| 5 to 10 | Senior Assistant Secretary / Under Secretary | Ministry files, policy drafting |
| 10 to 15 | Deputy Secretary, Additional DC | Programme management, field leadership |
| 15 to 20 | Joint Secretary, DC | Policy, district leadership |
| 20 and above | Additional Secretary, Secretary, Divisional Commissioner | Strategy, national programmes |

*A typical path, not a guarantee. Promotion depends on service rules, vacancies and board decisions.*

## Plan your own path (5-minute worksheet)

Copy these five lines and fill them in today:

1. **My age on the next cut-off date:** ___ (must be 32 or under)
2. **My cadre choices:** 1) Administration 2) ___ 3) ___
3. **Three weakest subjects:** ___, ___, ___
4. **Daily written-practice minutes:** ___ (aim for 60 to 90)
5. **My plan B if I do not get a cadre:** ___

Then take the free skill test on this page and compare the result with line 3.

## Career shifts: where officers move

- **Field administration to ministry posts** (and back), as postings rotate.
- **Administration to local government, land or planning roles** on deputation.
- **Government to the UN or development agencies** after study and experience abroad.
- **Government to academia or policy research** with a PhD.
- **Government to law or consultancy** after retirement or early exit.

## Where will you find more peace of mind?

No cadre is free of pressure, and we have no survey to rank them. Field administration carries real decision-making, public pressure, transfers and long hours during floods and elections. Secretariat postings tend to be file-heavy and more predictable. Three habits protect your peace in any posting: clean, documented decisions, a clear line between office and family time, and a few honest colleagues or mentors you can talk to.

## Faith and history: the trust of office

**The Quran.** Surah An-Nisa 4:58 tells believers to deliver trusts to those they are due and, when judging between people, to judge with justice ([read it on quran.com](https://quran.com/4/58)). A public post is an amanah.

**Hadith.** The Prophet (peace be upon him) said that each of you is a shepherd and each is responsible for his flock (Sahih al-Bukhari 893; Sahih Muslim 1829). An officer's flock is every citizen who walks into the office.

**History.** BCS (Administration) is described as the successor of the generalist cadre that was once called the steel frame of the British civil service. The first post of a new officer is Assistant Commissioner in the field on a two-year probation.

## Your contribution to the nation

An AC (Land) decides on mutation applications, land tax and khas land that affect families' homes and livelihoods. A fair, fast decision protects a widow's inheritance, a farmer's plot and a small business's premises. At the Secretariat, a clear note can save months of delay on a school, a bridge or a relief programme. Honest, prompt service at this level is a daily act of nation building.

## Your contribution to the world

Administration officers learn project management, disaster coordination and public finance on the job. Many go on to master's programmes abroad, development agencies and international organisations. Officers who coordinate flood and cyclone response build skills that international bodies value.

## If you do not get BCS Administration

- **Other BCS cadres.** The same exam leads to Police, Foreign Affairs, Taxation, Customs, Audit and others. Choose second and third options you genuinely want.
- **Non-cadre posts through BPSC.** In the 50th BCS there were 395 non-cadre posts (Grades 9 to 12).
- **Other government exams** such as banks and autonomous bodies.
- **Private sector and development jobs**, where policy writing and project skills matter.

## Research opportunities

- Topics with real need: land records and mutation delays, mobile courts, upazila governance, disaster response coordination, promotion and cadre policy, digital service delivery.
- Where to publish and learn: public administration and political science departments, BPATC programmes and policy think tanks.
- Path: a strong master's thesis, a research assistant post, then MPhil or PhD.

## Whom to follow and learn from

Follow institutions: [BPSC](https://www.bpsc.gov.bd), the [Ministry of Public Administration](https://mopa.gov.bd), [BPATC](https://bpatc.gov.bd) and the Ministry of Land. Treat coaching centre promises and social media rank claims with caution.

## Where do I find circulars?

- BPSC's official site: [bpsc.gov.bd](https://www.bpsc.gov.bd).
- Teletalk's BPSC application portal: bpsc.teletalk.com.bd.
- Daily newspapers' job pages (cross-check every date and number with the circular).

**No lobbying.** Tadbir during the application process is treated as grounds for disqualification.

## How should I write my profile and CV?

BCS does not choose candidates from a CV. Marks decide. But a short, honest profile helps in the viva, in backup applications and in scholarship forms.

| Weak line | Better line |
|---|---|
| Interested in public service. | Volunteered 120 hours at a union digital centre and wrote a 10-page report on service delays. |
| Leader. | Led a 12-member student relief team after a flood; raised and accounted for every taka. |
| Good writing. | Published 6 opinion pieces and wrote a 4,000-word thesis on local government. |

*Use only real, provable figures.*

Build yours free with the HereWeGrow CV Builder.

## What are the common mistakes?

- Putting too many unrealistic cadres on the choice list, or none you actually want.
- Skipping written practice.
- Weak English or maths because "I will fix it later".
- Giving textbook answers in the viva instead of your own examples.
- Having no plan B.
- Believing rumours about marks or posts instead of the circular.

## Changelog

- **19 Nov 2026:** Added dated key facts, question-style headings and this changelog. No figures changed.
- **18 Nov 2026:** First version.
- Next planned review: when the 52nd BCS circular is published.

growth_plan.y1: Download the latest circular and syllabus, fix your weakest two subjects, practise timed Bangla and English writing daily, study Bangladesh Affairs with a focus on the Constitution, local government and land administration, and apply when the circular opens.
growth_plan.y2: Clear the preliminary comfortably, build written-exam speed, prepare viva answers using your own district and real leadership examples, and keep a backup route moving.
growth_plan.y3: Sit written and viva with a full revision cycle; if selected, prepare for foundation training and the basic land management course; if not, use your plan B and re-apply within the age limit.

test.q: A rectangular government plot is 60 m by 45 m. What is its area?

options: The committee announce its decision yesterday.
The committee announcing its decision yesterday.
The committee has announce its decision yesterday.
The committee announced its decision yesterday.
test.explain: A past-tense action with 'yesterday' needs the simple past: announced.

test.q: A local leader asks you, as an AC (Land), to quietly skip the legal steps on a land case. The best action is to:
options: Skip the steps to avoid trouble
Follow the law, record the request and inform your superior
Ask the leader for a favour in return
Delay the file and say nothing
test.explain: Public trust requires lawful, documented decisions and honest reporting.

cv_template_notes: BCS does not select by CV, so use a clean one-page academic-style HWG layout (single column, no heavy graphics) for your viva profile, backup applications and scholarships. Lead with education and results, then leadership, volunteering and any public-service or research work. Add real numbers (people led, hours served, reports written). Keep it to one page. File name: YourName_BCS_Administration_Aspirant_CV.pdf. Use only facts you can prove in a viva.
cover_letter_md:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the [position] advertised on [site/date]. I hold a [degree] from [university] and have strong Bangla and English writing, research and people-management skills built while preparing for the BCS Administration cadre. In [project/volunteering role] I [one provable result, e.g. led a 12-member team that ran a flood relief drive and accounted for every taka].

My CV is attached as a PDF. I would be glad to attend an interview.

Sincerely,

interview_qs: Why do you want to join the Administration cadre? (Tip: Give a specific reason from real experience; talk about the work, not power or status.)
What does an AC (Land) do in a typical week? (Tip: Mention mutation, land development tax, government land and mobile courts.)
What is mutation (namjari) and why does it matter to ordinary people? (Tip: Use a family land example; show you understand delays and fairness.)
What would you do if a powerful person pressured you to break a rule? (Tip: Follow the law, document, inform your superior, stay polite.)
Tell us about your district and its main administrative problems. (Tip: Two facts, two problems, one realistic solution.)
How would you lead a team of staff older than you? (Tip: Respect, clear tasks, listening, and fairness; give a real example.)
What is the difference between field administration and the Secretariat? (Tip: Field is delivery to citizens; the Secretariat makes and tracks policy.)
Why not Police or another cadre? (Tip: Show you know the other cadre; explain your fit with Administration.)
How would you handle a flood emergency in your upazila? (Tip: Warning, shelters, relief lists, coordination, transparency in distribution.)
What is good governance and how can an AC apply it? (Tip: Transparency, accountability, participation, rule of law; one practical step each.)
How do you handle stress and long hours? (Tip: Share a real habit: planning, rest, and talking to a mentor.)
Describe a time you led or organised people. (Tip: Situation, action, result in numbers if possible.)
What recent reform in the civil service do you know about? (Tip: Name a real change (age limit 32, viva 100 marks, new pay scale) and give a balanced view.)
What will you do if you are not selected this time? (Tip: Show a calm plan B; do not sound defeated.)
Do you have any questions for us? (Tip: Ask about training or learning, not about pay or posting.)
